# Results — Study 948 (Capture Ratio) on the real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Fourteen US income ETFs —
covered-call writers and dividend-tilt funds — scored on **up-capture**, **down-capture**
and their difference (the **capture spread**) against the benchmark each fund is marketed
against (SPY / QQQ / IWM), on **monthly total returns** (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True` —
these funds pay most of their return out as distributions, so a price-only tape would be
meaningless). Cash leg = **BIL** (1-3 month T-bills). Every Sharpe race is
excess-of-cash on both sides. As-of **2026-06-30** — the partial current month is dropped.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | Monthly obs | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 income ETFs, SPY / QQQ / IWM, BIL | 2007-06-30 → 2026-06-30 | 327 month-ends (ragged: 46–229 per fund) | Fingerprint `01c183fa5741` |

Per-fund windows start at each fund's own inception (PBP 2008-01, DVY/VYM 2007-06 gated by
BIL's 2007 inception, SPYI 2022-09). Funds are scored on their own history rather than
truncated to a common window, which would throw away eighteen years of PBP to accommodate
a 2022 launch.

## Before anything else: one corporate action the vendor tape had missed

The screen in [`data.split_artifacts`](../capture_ratio/data.py) sweeps every daily close
for one-day price ratios that land on a real share-count factor (3:2, 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 5:1,
10:1 and their reverse twins, matched to 3%). Across all eighteen series it finds exactly
one:

| Ticker | Date | One-day ratio | Read as | Repaired |
|---|---|--:|---|---|
| NUSI | 2025-02-18 | **2.000000** | 1-for-2 reverse split | yes |

An exact ×2.000000 with no move in QQQ is a share count, not a return, and
`auto_adjust=True` had not backed it out. Left in, it is a **+100% month** for NUSI, and it
was doing an enormous amount of work:

| NUSI | Down-capture | Spread | CAPM alpha | Traded spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Raw (contaminated) | **−0.309** | **+0.939** | +185.6 bps/mo (*t* = +1.25) | +331.5 bps/mo |
| Repaired | +0.466 | +0.164 | +33.6 bps/mo (*t* = +1.43) | +53.0 bps/mo |

Every number below runs on the **repaired** tape. This matters for the headline: on the raw
tape NUSI was the one fund whose bootstrap CI excluded zero, so the panel read "13 of 14".
Repaired, it is **14 of 14**, and the cross-sectional mean spread moves from +0.051 to
−0.004. `load_prices(repair_splits=False)` reproduces the contaminated version.

## The scorecard — up-capture, down-capture, spread

Months are partitioned by the **benchmark's** sign. `conv` is the Henriksson-Merton
convexity coefficient `b_up − b_dn` on excess-of-cash returns (the spread's regression
twin) with its HAC (Newey-West, 6 lags) *t*. CIs are 95% circular block bootstrap
(2,000 draws, 3-month blocks) on the spread. **P(>0)** is the share of bootstrap draws
with a positive spread.

| Fund | Bench | n | From | Up | Down | **Spread** | 95% CI | P(>0) | conv | *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| QYLD | QQQ | 150 | 2014-01 | 0.497 | 0.559 | **−0.062** | [−0.21, +0.11] | 0.23 | −0.35 | **−2.62** |
| JEPQ | QQQ | 49 | 2022-06 | 0.712 | 0.689 | +0.023 | [−0.13, +0.24] | 0.64 | −0.44 | **−5.58** |
| NUSI | QQQ | 78 | 2020-01 | 0.630 | 0.466 | +0.164 | [−0.03, +0.39] | 0.95 | −0.20 | −1.65 |
| XYLD | SPY | 156 | 2013-07 | 0.641 | 0.711 | **−0.070** | [−0.22, +0.10] | 0.20 | −0.35 | **−2.14** |
| JEPI | SPY | 73 | 2020-06 | 0.592 | 0.571 | +0.021 | [−0.16, +0.20] | 0.60 | −0.14 | −0.72 |
| PBP | SPY | 222 | 2008-01 | 0.554 | 0.614 | **−0.060** | [−0.19, +0.09] | 0.21 | −0.37 | **−3.69** |
| DIVO | SPY | 114 | 2017-01 | 0.772 | 0.729 | +0.042 | [−0.10, +0.19] | 0.73 | +0.01 | +0.07 |
| SPYI | SPY | 46 | 2022-09 | 0.745 | 0.720 | +0.026 | [−0.05, +0.16] | 0.71 | −0.36 | **−5.49** |
| SCHD | SPY | 176 | 2011-11 | 0.860 | 0.839 | +0.020 | [−0.18, +0.24] | 0.56 | −0.09 | −0.69 |
| VYM | SPY | 229 | 2007-06 | 0.865 | 0.873 | −0.008 | [−0.14, +0.13] | 0.46 | −0.10 | −1.23 |
| DVY | SPY | 229 | 2007-06 | 0.800 | 0.819 | −0.018 | [−0.24, +0.21] | 0.46 | −0.21 | −1.39 |
| SPHD | SPY | 164 | 2012-11 | 0.713 | 0.754 | −0.041 | [−0.34, +0.27] | 0.39 | −0.28 | −1.16 |
| NOBL | SPY | 152 | 2013-11 | 0.822 | 0.894 | **−0.072** | [−0.28, +0.13] | 0.24 | −0.15 | −0.85 |
| RYLD | IWM | 86 | 2019-05 | 0.565 | 0.593 | −0.028 | [−0.21, +0.20] | 0.43 | −0.53 | **−3.15** |

- **Funds with a convexity *t* ≥ +2 (nominal): 0 of 14.** Clearing the Bonferroni bar for
  fourteen simultaneous tests (|*t*| ≥ **2.91**): **0**.
- **Funds with a convexity *t* ≤ −2 (genuinely concave): 6** — QYLD, JEPQ, XYLD, PBP,
  SPYI, RYLD. Every one of them writes options. They deliver exactly the payoff they sold.
- Cross-sectional spread: median **−0.013**, mean −0.004, min −0.072, max +0.164 (NUSI).
  The bootstrap CI covers zero for **14 of 14** funds.
- **Up-capture ≈ down-capture ≈ beta, for every fund.** The whole panel sits within a few
  points of the 45° line. These products are low-beta index positions, not convex ones.

## What the spread actually measures — the fund-matched null

The capture spread is a difference of two ratios of sample means, so it does not read zero
when the truth is zero. Two separate statements, and they must not be mixed:

**(a) Unconditional — the estimator in general.** Score the panel on 20 synthetic worlds in
which every fund is, by construction, **plain linear beta** (true capture spread exactly
0.000 for all 140 fund-panels):

| Measure | Mean | Median | SD | Positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Arithmetic capture spread | **+0.111** | +0.081 | 0.120 | **82%** |
| HM convexity coefficient | −0.003 | −0.006 | 0.071 | ~50% |

With a truth of exactly zero the industry ratio reads positive four times in five. The
regression twin does not. **This +0.111 is a property of the estimator when the benchmark
path is itself random, and it must NOT be subtracted from a real-tape spread** — a real
spread is computed on *one* realised benchmark path, and conditioning on that path removes
most of the bias. Doing the subtraction anyway would overstate the case by about 3×.

**(b) Conditional — each fund against its own sample.**
[`strategy.matched_null_spread`](../capture_ratio/strategy.py) rebuilds each fund 1,000
times as a **zero-convexity twin** — the fund's own beta and residual vol (circular block
bootstrap of the OLS residuals), on the **real** benchmark and cash paths — and re-scores
each replicate with the same estimator:

| Fund | Observed | Null(β) | Excess | *p* | Null(α,β) | Excess |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| QYLD | −0.062 | +0.031 | −0.093 | 0.886 | −0.058 | −0.004 |
| JEPQ | +0.023 | +0.052 | −0.029 | 0.644 | +0.069 | −0.046 |
| NUSI | +0.164 | +0.047 | +0.117 | 0.127 | +0.185 | −0.021 |
| XYLD | −0.070 | +0.023 | −0.093 | 0.897 | −0.077 | +0.006 |
| JEPI | +0.021 | +0.054 | −0.032 | 0.640 | +0.040 | −0.019 |
| PBP | −0.060 | +0.024 | −0.084 | 0.919 | −0.077 | +0.017 |
| DIVO | +0.042 | +0.028 | +0.015 | 0.429 | +0.057 | −0.015 |
| SPYI | +0.026 | +0.063 | −0.037 | 0.745 | +0.053 | −0.028 |
| SCHD | +0.020 | +0.011 | +0.009 | 0.447 | +0.034 | −0.013 |
| VYM | −0.008 | +0.009 | −0.016 | 0.614 | −0.009 | +0.002 |
| DVY | −0.018 | +0.011 | −0.030 | 0.619 | −0.027 | +0.009 |
| SPHD | −0.041 | +0.014 | −0.054 | 0.644 | −0.067 | +0.027 |
| NOBL | −0.072 | +0.008 | −0.080 | 0.783 | −0.063 | −0.009 |
| RYLD | −0.028 | +0.036 | −0.063 | 0.732 | −0.027 | −0.000 |

- **Null(β)** is a plain scaled index position: zero alpha, zero convexity. **0 of 14**
  funds' spreads reach even *p* < 0.05 against it (smallest *p* = **0.127**, NUSI). The
  median excess spread is **−0.035** — measurably below the ruler's own reading on nothing,
  but a third of what the unconditional bias would have implied.
- **Null(α,β)** keeps the fund's own fitted alpha and is a **decomposition, not a test**: it
  reproduces the observed spread to a median error of **0.014** (max 0.046) for all fourteen
  funds. The capture spread carries **no information beyond (alpha, beta)** — it is a
  re-encoding of the CAPM fit, not an independent measurement of payoff shape.
- **Caveat, stated because it cuts against us:** Null(β) also fires on a perfectly *linear*
  fund carrying a positive alpha, because alpha divides by a positive mean up-month and by a
  **negative** mean down-month and so lands in the spread twice with the same sign. A small
  *p* there would mean "beats a scaled index", not "is convex". Convexity as such is the HM
  column, whose free intercept separates the two. Both facts are tested
  (`test_alpha_alone_manufactures_a_positive_capture_spread`,
  `test_matched_null_detects_a_genuinely_convex_fund`).

## Is it just beta? CAPM alpha (excess-of-cash, HAC 6 lags)

| Fund | Beta | Alpha (bps/mo) | *t* | Kink intercept (bps/mo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| QYLD | 0.52 | −18.6 | −1.24 | +51.6 |
| JEPQ | 0.65 | +3.8 | +0.22 | +99.4 |
| NUSI | 0.54 | +33.6 | +1.43 | +81.0 |
| XYLD | 0.68 | −17.4 | −1.17 | +40.4 |
| JEPI | 0.56 | −2.6 | −0.21 | +23.3 |
| PBP | 0.63 | −18.8 | −1.56 | +48.8 |
| DIVO | 0.73 | +5.7 | +0.45 | +3.9 |
| SPYI | 0.71 | −1.6 | −0.17 | +58.9 |
| SCHD | 0.83 | +3.8 | +0.23 | +18.4 |
| VYM | 0.87 | −3.3 | −0.28 | +14.7 |
| DVY | 0.83 | −7.1 | −0.34 | +30.1 |
| SPHD | 0.77 | −13.9 | −0.48 | +31.1 |
| NOBL | 0.84 | −12.4 | −0.81 | +12.7 |
| RYLD | 0.58 | −16.5 | −0.61 | +120.1 |

**Max |*t*| on alpha across the whole panel: 1.56** (PBP, negative). Not one fund adds
anything measurable beyond a smaller position in its index. The **kink intercept** is large
and positive for the option-writers (QYLD +52, RYLD +120 bps/mo) — that is the premium
collected in a flat month, and it is *not* alpha: a kinked fit pushes the intercept up
mechanically, and the same fit shows the fund giving that premium straight back through a
truncated up-beta.

**1 of 14 funds beats its own benchmark on excess-of-cash Sharpe**, and it is NUSI, on 78
months, by a margin that is not significant in the direction that matters: the HAC *t* on
its monthly excess-return difference is **−1.28**, i.e. NUSI's mean excess return is *below*
QQQ's and the Sharpe win comes entirely from lower volatility. Six funds are behind at
|*t*| ≥ 2. The drawdown column is where the products *do* deliver: eleven of fourteen cut
the worst loss — but so does holding less of the index, which is what they are.

## Robustness

**Era cut (split 2021-01-01, ≥ 24 months each side) and rank persistence.** Nine funds
qualify:

| Fund | Early spread | Late spread |
|---|--:|--:|
| QYLD | −0.107 | −0.016 |
| XYLD | −0.193 | +0.052 |
| PBP | −0.112 | +0.073 |
| DIVO | +0.017 | +0.057 |
| SCHD | +0.025 | +0.002 |
| VYM | −0.037 | +0.092 |
| DVY | −0.025 | +0.112 |
| SPHD | −0.116 | +0.034 |
| NOBL | −0.024 | −0.125 |

**Spearman rho = −0.117 (p = 0.756, n = 9); sign agreement 44%** — worse than a coin. The
early era's capture ranking carries **no** information about the late era's. Five of the
nine funds flip the sign of their spread outright. The scorecard describes a sample, not a
fund. (n = 9 is small; the point is the absence of evidence *for* persistence in the only
cut the data supports, not a precise estimate of rho.)

**Benchmark-assignment sweep (ASSUMPTION).** Re-running the whole panel with **SPY** forced
as everyone's benchmark: median spread −0.003, still **0** funds with convexity *t* ≥ +2,
5 with *t* ≤ −2. Only the four non-S&P funds move (QYLD −0.062 → +0.002, JEPQ +0.023 →
+0.140, NUSI +0.164 → +0.309, RYLD −0.028 → −0.173) and none of them crosses into
significance. The verdict does not depend on the map.

**Convention sweep (arithmetic vs geometric).** Under Morningstar's compounding definition
**every single fund's spread falls**, and thirteen of fourteen turn negative (QYLD −0.062 →
−0.178, RYLD −0.028 → −0.171, DIVO +0.042 → −0.038; NUSI +0.164 → +0.030 is the only
survivor and it is barely above zero). The handful of mildly positive arithmetic spreads do
not survive a change of convention.

## Tradability — the beta-neutral traded spread

Long the fund, short `beta_hat` of the benchmark, remainder in cash. `beta_hat` is the
36-month rolling OLS slope **through month *t***, held over month ***t*+1** — the study's
one and only execution lag. Costs 5 bps one-way × NAV on the notional turned over; the
short index leg pays borrow.

| Fund | n | Gross (bps/mo) | *t* | Net @ 5 bps + 100 bps borrow | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| NUSI | 42 | +53.0 | +1.60 | +48.1 | +1.45 |
| JEPQ | 13 | +13.2 | +0.36 | +7.3 | +0.20 |
| DVY | 193 | +0.8 | +0.04 | −6.0 | −0.29 |
| VYM | 193 | −0.5 | −0.04 | −7.9 | −0.64 |
| DIVO | 78 | −1.4 | −0.08 | −7.8 | −0.45 |
| SCHD | 140 | −4.1 | −0.22 | −11.6 | −0.62 |
| PBP | 186 | −18.9 | −1.55 | −24.0 | −1.96 |
| QYLD | 114 | −24.2 | −1.36 | −28.8 | −1.62 |
| NOBL | 116 | −25.5 | −1.47 | −33.0 | −1.91 |
| SPHD | 128 | −27.5 | −0.87 | −34.2 | −1.09 |
| XYLD | 120 | −27.9 | −1.87 | −34.1 | −2.28 |
| RYLD | 50 | −35.7 | −1.74 | −40.2 | −1.94 |
| JEPI | 37 | −39.9 | −2.16 | −45.0 | −2.44 |

(SPYI has too little history for a 36-month rolling beta.) The **largest gross spread in the
whole panel, ignoring any history floor, is NUSI at +53.0 bps/month on 42 months — *t* =
+1.60, short of the bar even before costs.** The best one with at least 60 months is
**DVY at +0.8 bps/month gross (*t* = +0.04)**, and its borrow sweep kills even that:

| Borrow | Net (bps/mo) | *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | +0.6 | +0.03 | +0.01 |
| 50 bps | −2.7 | −0.13 | −0.04 |
| 100 bps | −6.0 | −0.29 | −0.08 |
| 200 bps | −12.7 | −0.62 | −0.18 |

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a **planted** cross-section (one genuinely convex fund, three genuinely concave, three
flat) the scorecard recovers the truth: correlation between measured and planted spread
**+0.912**, and the HM test flags **1 positive / 3 negative** of 7 funds — exactly the
planted structure. On the **null** (every fund plain linear beta) |*t*| ≥ 2 fires on
**3 of 56** fund-tests across 8 seeds, against the ~2.8 a nominal 5% rate predicts. The
harness detects convexity when it is there and stays quiet when it is not, so the real-tape
zero is a property of the funds and not of the measurement.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The marquee income-fund claim — "give up a little upside, avoid a lot
  of downside" — does **not** hold for a single one of the fourteen funds. Zero funds have
  a positive convexity coefficient at even a nominal |*t*| ≥ 2, let alone at the
  Bonferroni bar of 2.91 that fourteen simultaneous tests demand; the bootstrap CI on the
  spread covers zero for **14 of 14**; against each fund's own zero-convexity twin, on its
  own sample and its own benchmark path, **0 of 14** reach *p* < 0.05 (smallest 0.127) and
  the median excess spread is **−0.035**; and the spread has **no rank persistence** across
  eras (rho = −0.117, p = 0.76, sign agreement 44%). The one largest positive (NUSI, +0.164)
  has a *negative* convexity coefficient, a CI that straddles zero, and needed an
  unadjusted reverse split removed before it stopped reading +0.939. What *is* robust runs
  the other way: six funds are significantly **concave** — and all six write options, so
  that is an accounting identity of selling calls, not a discovered effect.
  **Survivorship:** the fourteen funds are those still listed on Yahoo's tape as of
  2026-06-30; the buy-write and high-dividend ETFs that closed over the same period are
  absent, so this scorecard is biased **in the funds' favour** and the true panel is worse
  than the table.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to buy and nothing to short. Every fund is a
  low-beta index position (beta 0.52–0.87) with **no alpha** — the largest |*t*| on alpha
  in the whole panel is 1.56, and it is *negative* — and **1 of 14** beats its own benchmark
  on excess-of-cash Sharpe, on lower vol rather than higher return (NUSI, HAC *t* on the
  monthly difference −1.28). The beta-neutral spread that would monetise the scorecard tops
  out at **+53.0 bps/month gross on 42 months (*t* = +1.60)** and, among funds with a real
  history, at **+0.8 bps/month (*t* = +0.04)** — which goes negative at 50 bps of borrow.
  The reduced drawdowns are real but are bought with beta, and an investor can buy the same
  reduction by holding less of the index at a fraction of the fee.
- **What the funds actually sell.** Not convexity: **beta reduction plus a distribution
  schedule**. The option premium shows up as a fat kink intercept (QYLD +52, RYLD +120
  bps/mo) and is handed straight back through a truncated up-beta. That is a fair trade,
  honestly priced — it is simply not the asymmetric one the marketing describes.
